entries.title: John 4:4
segments: Samaria. A province of Palestine between Galilee on the north and Judea on the south.  Its greatest length is about forty miles and its grestest width about forty-five miles.  Its western boundary is the Mediterranean Sea and its eastern the River Jordan.  The Samaritans were a mixed race, but with a considerable Jewish element.  In the time of our Lord they worshipped mainly according to the Jewish faith, but rejected the Old Testament with the exception of the first five books or Pentateuch.  They believed that the only place of the Temple was on Mount Gerizim.  This was a prominent cause of their dislike of the Jews, who despised them.

entries.title: John 4:5
segments: A city of Samaria, called Sychar. Now identified by some scholars with Askar, near Shechem.

entries.title: John 4:6
segments:
Jacob's well was there. It is there still.
 

 
Being wearied. His human nature, though without sin, was touched with our infirmities.
 

 
The sixth hour. About noon.

entries.title: John 4:9
segments: No dealings. That is, no important or intimate communications.  This was particularly true of the Jews of Judea.  Our Lord's disciples, being Galileans, were less prejudiced.  Hence they went to a Samaritan town to buy food.  Jesus himself had spoken in a friendly manner to the woman, before he began to reprove her for her manner of life.  His ministry in Samaria was as full of love and compassionate warning as it was in any other part of Palestine.

entries.title: John 4:11
segments: Whence then hast thou that living water? The woman had taken his words literally, thinking he meant spring water as purer than the water in the well.

entries.title: John 4:14
segments: A well of water springing up unto everlasting life. A fountain of spiritual power, satisfying every righteous aspiration and hunger of the soul.

entries.title: John 4:15
segments: The woman saith unto him. It is difficult to say whether sincerity or mockery prompted her reply.

entries.title: John 4:16
segments: Go, call thy husband. This command of Jesus suddenly revealed the woman's frailty and compelled her alarmed attention.  He wished to convince her of sin and show her the way to righteousness.  Her trifling answers were no longer possible.

entries.title: John 4:17
segments: I have no husband. A true answer, literally taken, though given with an intention to deceive.

entries.title: John 4:18
segments: Whom thou now hast is not thy husband. Jesus reveals her past life, but there is no word of severe reproof.  He was always gentle and compassionate with sinners of her class.  See

entries.title: John 4:19
segments: Thou art a prophet. The woman felt that concealment was vain.  In addressing Jesus as a prophet she also saw a chance to avoid further humiliation by suggesting a different subject.

entries.title: John 4:20
segments: Worshipped in this mountain. The Samaritans believed that Mount Gerizim was the proper place for the Temple.  This was a standing dispute between them and the Jews.  Doubtless the woman thought that Jesus would have something important to say about it.

entries.title: John 4:21
segments:
Woman, believe me. Seeing that she was ashamed, Jesus permitted her to forget her fault for the moment and proceeded to instruct her.
 

 
The hour cometh, and now is, etc. A blessed and glorious prophecy, in whose fulfillment all the strife and pettiness proceeding from unessential and limiting forms of worship shall pass away forever.  Christ shows the woman that in time there shall be no exclusive place of worship, though for her and in her time Jerusalem is better than Mount Gerizim.  'Now is' refers to the few who already worshipped the Father in spirit and in truth, valuing symbols for their educational uses, and seeing through incense and the smoke of sacrifice to the heart of the holy mystery of religion.

entries.title: John 4:26
segments: I that speak unto thee am he. Christ's willingness in making himself known as Messiah to the woman was in marked contrast to his refusal to permit a similar declaration among the Jews.  But the Samaritans looked for a religious deliverer and had no political hopes.  Even if they had known that he who thus spoke to the woman was the Messiah, they would not have interrupted his spiritual mission to make him king.

entries.title: John 4:27
segments: Speaking with a woman. The disciples marveled because it was not customary for a Jewish rabbi to speak to a woman publicly.

entries.title: John 4:35
segments:
Say not ye, There are yet four months, etc.  This reference to the harvest, which is not figurative, indicates that the time was about the middle of December, as harvest did not begin until about he middle of April.
 

 
Look on the fields, etc.  Alluding most probably to the Samaritans who were coming from all sides to hear him.

entries.title: John 4:37
segments: One soweth, and another reapeth. Christ sowed the seed; the apostles and all generations after them were to reap the grain.

entries.title: John 4:38
segments: Others. Meaning Christ himself.

entries.title: John 4:42
segments: The Savior of the world. The reasons for this conviction are clear.  The Samaritans were not looking for a deliverer from the Romans and were therefore more disposed to listen to the words of one who spoke only of spiritual things.  The conversion of the woman led many to seek him.  In simple faith they accepted him as the Savior of the world because they believed him to be their Messiah.

entries.title: John 4:43
segments: He went forth from thence into Galilee. This was the beginning of his Galilean ministry.  His previous appearance at Cana in Galilee was an episode of his Judean ministry.

entries.title: John 4:44
segments: In his own country. Judea, the country of his birth.

entries.title: John 4:46
segments:
:54
 
A certain nobleman, whose son was sick. The miracle of the healing of the nobleman's son is narrated in these verses.
 

 
Capernaum. About twenty miles from Cana.
 

 
Except ye see signs and wonders, etc.  These words were spoken to test the nobleman's faith.  He seemed to think it necessary for Jesus to be present at the bedside of his son in order to heal him.  He asked Jesus the second time to go down to Capernaum.
 

 
Go thy way; thy son liveth. A critical instant for the distressed father.  If he had hesitated, his son might have died.
 

 
The man believed. His faith must have been immediate and entire; he showed this by starting on his return apparently without a word.  But the strongest proof of it was the testimony of his servants that the fever left his son at the time when Jesus spoke the healing word.  The man's faith thought not of distance or of any limitation.
 

 
The seventh hour. One o'clock in the afternoon.
